body.text:
OSSIFICATION ZONES
RESERVE / QUIESCENT ZONE: This is the zone farthest away from
the ossification front. Little cellular activity or cell division is
occurring.
PROLIFERATIVE ZONE: Chondrocytes are multiplying and arrange
themselves in long parallel columns: This is the main zone
responsible for growth of the long axis of the bone.
MATURATION ZONE: Chondrocytes are hypertrophying and
secreting alkaline phosphatase.
CALCIFICATION ZONE: Matrix around the hypertrophied cells
solidifying, trapping the chondrocytes in the matrix. Chondrocytes
are dying here.
BONE DEPOSITION ZONE: The chondrocytes die once calcification
is complete, due to no nutrients. New osteoblasts are recruited
from the blood supply in the vascular bud.

Formation of bone directly from osteoblasts, with no cartilage
intermediate.
Mesenchymal Cells --> Osteoblasts
Osteoblasts secrete the Osteoid Matrix.

trapping themselves in it, and thereby forming Osteocytes.
NEUROCRANIUM: Flat bones form by intramembranous
ossification. The bone spicules coalesce in the calcified matrix to
form parallel, strong, trabeculae that make up flat bones.
Exceptions: Occipital, Temporal, and Sphenoid bones are both
endochondral and intramembranous.

Histology difference of White and Grey Matter
The CNS has a characteristic tissue arrangement called
grey matter and white matter. Grey matter contains the
cell bodies (perikarya) of neurons, the supporting cells
(neuroglia), and unmyelinated dendrites. White matter
does not contain any cell bodies but mostly contains
myelinated nerve fibers.

body.text:
Filtration apparatus
The FILTRATION BARRIER separates urinary space from the blood in the
capillaries.
a- Podocyte have bundles of actin microfilaments in their cytoplasm, giving them
the contractile capacity. From its cell body, several primary processes arise forming
numerous secondary processes called PEDICELS that embrace capillaries of
glomerulus. Secondary processes are in direct contact with basal lamina. Cell
bodies and primary processes do not touch basement membrane.
b- Basement membrane: The BM is located between fenestrated endothelial cells
of the capillaries and the podocytes. The basement membrane made up of lamina
densa sandwiched by lamina rara that contains fibronectin binds them to the cells.
Lamina densa is made up of type IV collagen and laminin with proteoglycan
heparin sulfate, restricts passage of anionic molecules. Glomerular basement
membrane is a selective macromolecular filter where lamina dense is a physical
filter and the lamina rara is a charge barrier.
c- Filtration slits: The slit is formed by interdigitation between secondary
processes of podocytes, bridged by diaphragm.

Bowman’s capsule
• Surrounds glomerulus
• consists of parietal layer of simple squamous epithelium reflected onto capillary tuft
to form the visceral layer creating renal space
• continued into the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT).
• The parietal layer of Bowman’s capsule changes into simple cuboidal or low
columnar epithelium toward the PCT and form the renal pole
• Visceral layer contained specialized cells called Podocyte or visceral epithelial
cells which extend their processes around the capillaries.

Juxtaglomerular apparatus
• Mesangial cell: Cells adhering to capillary walls.
-contractile and have receptors for angiotensin II (activation reduces flow)
-have receptors for Natriuretic factor produced by cardiac atrial cells (vasodilator)
-give structural support to the glomerulus
-synthesize Extracellular matrix
-endocytose and dispose of immune-complex molecules trapped by glomerular
basement membrane,
-produce chemical mediators such as cytokines and prostaglandins.
-in vascular pole, these are called extraglomerular mesangial cells.
• Macula densa: Lying adjacent to the Afferent and efferent arterioles and mesangial
cells, the lining cells of the straight distal convoluted tubules become tall and closely
packed, and their nuclei are apically located.
• Juxtaglomerular cells: These cells are the smooth muscle of the wall of the
afferent and “sometimes the efferent” arterioles. They have a spherical nucleus and
their cytoplasm contains secretory granules “renin”.

have acidophilic cytoplasm due to numerous mitochondria
has abundant lysosomes and vesicles, cell apex has abundant microvilli forming brush border
surrounded by peritubular capillaries.
Loop of Henle:
U-shaped structure consisting of descending and ascending limbs
each has thick (lined by low cuboidal) and thin segments (squamous epithelium)
Thin descending limb is permeable to water; ascending limb is impermeable to water.
Distal convoluted tubule:
lined with shorter cuboidal epithelial cells and lack brush border
connects with the vascular pole where it is modified; cells become columnar, nuclei closely
packed together and apically located  called MACULA DENSA
Macula densa cells are sensitive to ionic content and water volume of tubular fluid, producing
molecular signals that promote liberation of enzyme RENIN from the smooth muscle of
afferent arteriole into the circulation.
In the DCT, there is ion exchange if aldosterone is present. Sodium is absorbed and K ions are
secreted

Collecting ducts
It is a large straight duct that widens gradually as it approaches tip of the medullary
pyramids. Two types of cuboidal epithelial cells line the CD; Principal and Intercalated cells
The principal has basal infolding and apical none motile cilium, act as mechanosensor,
absorbs Na and water and secrete K.
The intercalated cells have apical microvilli, secrete H+ and HCO3- .

body.text:
Urethra
The urethra is a fibromuscular tube that conveys urine from the bladder to
exterior through external urethral orifice. The lining epithelium changes
throughout the length of the urethra.
Male urethra: serves as a terminal duct for urine and genital system.
1- Prostatic urethra: lined by transitional epithelium, many prostatic ducts empty
into this segment.
2- Membranous urethra: Lined by stratified or pseudostratified columnar
epithelium.
3- Penile urethra: opens at the glans penis, surrounded by corpus spongiosum
throughout the length of the penis. Lined with pseudostratified columnar
epithelium continued to become stratified squamous epithelium toward the
distal end where it continued with the skin of the penis.
Female urethra: is short 3-5 cm, runs from the urinary bladder to vestibule of the
vagina. The urethra is lined with stratified squamous epithelium which later
becomes keratinized near the urethral meatus. Lamina propria is highly
vascularized and has inner smooth and outer striated muscles.
